prompt: For a nonzero unsigned int `x`, what does `x & (x - 1)` change?

options.text: It subtracts one without changing any other bits
options.explanation: Subtraction changes lower zeros too; AND removes those new ones.

options.text: It retains only the lowest set bit
It clears the lowest set bit while preserving higher set bits
options.explanation: Correct. Subtraction clears that one and sets lower zeros; AND with the original removes the new lower ones.

options.text: It always clears the entire value
options.explanation: That happens only when the original had one set bit.

workedExample: Subtracting one reaches the lowest set bit, turning it off and turning lower zeros on. The original had zeros in those lower positions, so AND clears them again. Higher positions are unchanged.

prompt: Two non-negative Python integers have the same highest set-bit position. One has only two set bits; the other has many. Which needs fewer iterations in the loop `while x: x &= x - 1`?

options.text: They always need the same number
options.explanation: The loop does not visit every position; it removes set bits.

options.text: The one with only two set bits
options.explanation: Correct. Each iteration clears exactly one set bit, so this input needs two iterations.

options.text: The one with more set bits
options.explanation: More set bits require more removals.

options.text: The one whose decimal spelling is shorter
options.explanation: Decimal formatting does not determine the loop's progress.

workedExample: Each iteration removes one set bit and the loop ends when none remain. Equal storage width or highest position therefore does not imply equal iteration counts. This describes iteration count; actual speed also depends on Python's arbitrary-precision operations.

prompt: For a nonzero unsigned int `i`, why does `i & -i` isolate the lowest set bit?

options.text: Negation preserves that bit while inverting the higher pattern
options.explanation: Correct. Invert-and-add-one carries through the original trailing zeros and restores the lowest one; AND removes the higher differences.

options.text: Negation simply clears the lowest set bit
options.explanation: That is the effect of `i & (i - 1)`, not negation.

options.text: Negation is identical to bitwise inversion
options.explanation: Unsigned negation requires inversion plus one, so it can overlap the original.

options.text: AND selects the highest position automatically
options.explanation: AND compares positions independently; the negated pattern creates the lowest-bit result.

workedExample: Follow the carry when adding one to the inverted pattern. It clears the trailing ones created from the original trailing zeros and stops at the original lowest set bit. That bit survives in both operands, while higher positions differ. Unsigned arithmetic supplies the required defined wraparound.
